set_schedule.name: Set schedule
set_schedule.description: Saves the periods to the chosen days of a timer programme on the heater. Each day is replaced and then read back. If the heater can't be reached, the change waits and is written when it is next reachable.

days.name: Days
days.description: The days that get these periods.

periods.name: Periods
periods.description: Up to 4 heating periods. To remove all heating periods from the chosen days, give an empty list ([]).

get_schedule.name: Get schedule
get_schedule.description: Returns each timer programme as the heater held it at the last read (read_at), the changes still waiting for the heater, and Home Assistant's backup copy.

restore_schedule.name: Restore schedule

heater_stalled.title: {name} stopped responding
heater_stalled.description: Home Assistant hasn't heard the heater for over a minute while its Bluetooth proxy is online: its Bluetooth has most likely stopped, and only a power cycle restarts it. If your installation has a mains isolator switch: switch it off, wait at least 5 seconds, then switch it on. If there is no isolator switch: switch off the circuit breaker or remove the fuse supplying the unit, wait at least 5 seconds, then switch it on. Home Assistant reconnects automatically. (A phone app connected to the heater also blocks it: the heater accepts one connection at a time.)

schedule_pending.title: {name}: schedule change waiting
schedule_pending.description: The heater couldn't be reached when its schedule was changed. Home Assistant keeps the change and writes it as soon as the heater answers again; until then the heater keeps running its previous schedule.

cloud_sign_in.title: Dimplex sign-in expired
cloud_sign_in.description: Dimplex no longer accepts Home Assistant's sign-in, so firmware updates can't be checked. Open a heater's settings and save its QR label again to sign in.
